comps.spec: Gear train in stand mixers: worm, bevel and planetary gears in a greased case. Housings and gears vary: some KitchenAid New Generation housings are plastic, and the Classic's worm gear is nylon

Speed control board: a plate of contact switches read from a centrifugal governor on the KitchenAid Classic, a control board (part 9706509) on the KitchenAid New Generation; the Blendtec Total has a logic board

Motor and gear bearings: two ball bearings (reported as 608RS size) on the Blendtec Total rotor; a sealed front armature bearing with oil-impregnated rear and beater-shaft bearings on the KitchenAid Classic
Variable speed dial on the Vitamix 5200, active only with the High/Variable switch on Variable; its electrical type is not stated
Mains cord with plug (three-prong earthed on the Vitamix 5200, polarised on Oster blenders) — good for repairs and extension leads
Speed sensor: a Hall effect sensor on the KitchenAid New Generation (part 9703312) or an inductive sensor on the Blendtec Total

Overload or thermal cut-out: the Blendtec Total's thermistor shuts the motor off at 130°C and the Vitamix 5200 shuts off on overheating (reset button underneath on 220/240V units) — never heat, bridge or rely on a salvaged one
